title: BJP Attacks Sonia Gandhi Over Babri Remark in Memoir Interviews
excerpt: BJP spokesmen Sudhanshu Trivedi and Pradeep Bhandari accused Congress of an 'anti-Ram' face after Sonia Gandhi said she cried watching the 1992 Babri Masjid demolition, days before her memoir 'Belonging' is published on November 10.
body:
• BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi said on Saturday, November 7, that Sonia Gandhi's remark that she cried watching the Babri Masjid demolition had again exposed what he called Congress's "anti-Ram" face.
  • The remarks came in interviews ahead of Gandhi's memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love, scheduled for publication on November 10, 2026.
  • Trivedi questioned when and on which television channel Gandhi had watched the December 6, 1992 demolition, and accused Congress of double standards over the Batla House encounter and national security.
  • Other BJP leaders, including Tarun Chugh and Pradeep Bhandari, widened the attack to the Emergency, the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and what Bhandari called vote-bank politics.

The BJP on Saturday launched a coordinated attack on Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi over her statement that she had cried witnessing the demolition of the Babri Masjid in Ayodhya on December 6, 1992, saying it had again exposed the "anti-Ram" face of Congress. The mosque stood at the site that is now home to the Ram temple in Ayodhya.

BJP spokesperson and Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi, addressing a press conference in New Delhi, accused the Congress leadership of double standards on national security, religious sentiments and women's rights, according to IANS reporting published by hi INDiA. "From Mahatma Gandhi's conception of Ram Rajya, Congress has now limited its memory to Babar," Trivedi said.

"The anti-Ram face of the Congress has once again been exposed. Sonia Gandhi sheds tears over the 1992 incident, but her compassion is never seen when it comes to terrorists and the killing of innocent people."

— Sudhanshu Trivedi, BJP spokesperson

What Gandhi said, and where

The BJP reaction followed interviews Gandhi gave ahead of the launch of her book, Belonging: A Journey of Love. In an interview with The Hindu ahead of the launch, she also said people are now beginning to be restless and recognising the damage, and, weighing in on the Emergency, she said it was done constitutionally, according to reporting on the BJP's response. The memoir is scheduled for publication on November 10, 2026.

The BJP's lines of attack

Trivedi questioned Gandhi's reported emotional response to the events of December 6, 1992, asking when and on which television channel she had watched the visuals, and arguing that Indian television was not broadcasting the demolition live throughout the day. Referring to the Batla House encounter, he alleged that Gandhi had expressed concern for the accused but had not shown comparable emotion for security personnel who died defending Parliament. He also contrasted Rajiv Gandhi's 1989 election campaign, which began from Ayodhya with a promise of 'Ram Rajya', with what he described as Sonia Gandhi's politics revolving around the Babri Masjid, Batla House and Gaza.

Senior BJP leader Tarun Chugh alleged that Congress's history has been one of dividing the country through caste, religion and vote-bank politics, and asked Gandhi to write about the scams under her party's rule, the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and the Bhopal gas tragedy. BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said: "Sonia Gandhi cried for Babri, Sonia Gandhi cried for Batla House, Sonia Gandhi will do anything for vote bank. Congress hates Hindus."

Why it is surfacing now

The exchange is tied to the memoir's release rather than to any new Ayodhya development: Gandhi's interviews have revisited the demolition, the Emergency and Congress's own record, and the BJP has used each to press its long-running charge that Congress practises appeasement politics. Trivedi also questioned the silence of Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra over allegations levelled against senior Congress leader Harak Singh Rawat. The reports read for this article carried no Congress rebuttal to Saturday's press conference; the party's response, and the memoir itself on November 10, are the next developments to watch.
